title: The British Conquest and the Revolt of 1857

questions.question: The East India Company was chartered on 31 December 1600 by:
questions.rationale: Elizabeth I granted the Company its charter in 1600; James I later sent Sir Thomas Roe to Jahangir's court, winning the farman for the Surat factory of 1613.

questions.question: Bombay came to the English Crown in 1661 as:
options: A battle prize from the Portuguese
The dowry of Catherine of Braganza
questions.rationale: Bombay arrived as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza on her marriage to Charles II; the Crown leased it to the Company in 1668.

questions.question: The Battle of Plassey (1757) was effectively decided by:
options: The betrayal of Mir Jafar, bought by the Company
A treaty with the Mughal emperor
questions.rationale: Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander Mir Jafar had been purchased with the Jagat Seth bankers brokering, so Plassey was won by conspiracy before it was won by arms.

questions.question: At Buxar (22 October 1764), Hector Munro defeated the 'triple alliance' of:
options: Nana Saheb, Tantia Tope, and Kunwar Singh
Haider Ali, the Nizam, and the French
Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula, and Shah Alam II
questions.rationale: The Company defeated Mir Qasim of Bengal, Awadh's Shuja-ud-Daula, and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II, leading to the Diwani grant of 1765.

questions.question: The Diwani of 1765 entitled the Company to:
options: The revenue rights of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa
Trade monopoly in all of Asia
questions.rationale: By the Treaty of Allahabad, Shah Alam II granted the Diwani — revenue collection of Bengal, Bihar, and Orissa — legalising Company rule of eastern India.

questions.question: The Subsidiary Alliance system, first accepted by Hyderabad in 1798, was introduced by:
questions.rationale: Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliances made rulers pay for British troops, host a Resident, and surrender their foreign policy — Hyderabad signed first.

questions.question: Under the Doctrine of Lapse, which state was annexed in 1853 after its ruler's adopted heir was refused recognition?
questions.rationale: Dalhousie annexed Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854) by refusing adopted heirs under the Doctrine of Lapse.

questions.question: The immediate trigger of the 1857 revolt was:
options: Rumours that Enfield rifle cartridges were greased with cow and pig fat
questions.rationale: Sepoys had to bite the new Enfield cartridge; rumours of cow and pig fat offended Hindu and Muslim sepoys alike. Mangal Pandey's outburst at Barrackpore (29 March 1857) opened the revolt.

questions.question: Match the centre of the revolt with its leader: which pair is correct?
questions.rationale: Jhansi's Rani Lakshmibai died fighting in June 1858; Delhi had Bahadur Shah Zafar, Kanpur had Nana Saheb and Tantia Tope, and Lucknow was held for Begum Hazrat Mahal's son.

questions.question: Which change followed the revolt's failure?
options: The Company's charter was renewed for thirty years
The Crown took direct rule under the Government of India Act 1858
The Doctrine of Lapse was extended
questions.rationale: The Act of 1858 ended Company rule, creating a Secretary of State and making the Governor-General the first Viceroy; Bahadur Shah's exile ended the Mughal title in 1862.
